5.2.0.title: NODE_GRID is now Null Grid
new: NODE_GRID is now called Null Grid. Same browser, new name: your settings, favorites, history, saved logins, Vault and sign-ins all came with it.
Ctrl+N opens a new window, with tabs of its own. Also in a tab's right-click menu, and by right-clicking NEW TAB.

Drag a tab out of the window to give it a window of its own, or drop it on another Null Grid window's tabs to move it there. Right-click a tab > Move to new window / Move to window does the same. The page keeps running while it moves.
Each window has its own tabs, panels, AI panel and radio. Settings, favorites, history, logins and downloads are shared by every window.
After an update restart, every window comes back with its own tabs.

5.1.7.title: Tabs on top
new: Settings > APPEARANCE > Tabs: put your tabs in a row across the top like other browsers. The sidebar shrinks to a rail one icon wide; history, downloads, vault and loadouts still open from it.
fixed: A YouTube video in the sidebar radio now fills its box, with no black bars above and below.
The Null Grid icon now fills its space on the taskbar like other apps: no black square around the blue frame.
Windows: a popped-out video no longer shows up as a second Null Grid button on the taskbar.

5.1.6.title: Security release
new: Not-secure warning: plain http sites stop at a warning first, with CLOSE, PROCEED, DON'T TRUST (logins never saved or filled), or PROCEED, I TRUST IT (remembered; logins work there). Your own computer is never warned.
Unlock to fill: with a PIN set, a small PIN box pops up when a sign-in page opens; type it and your login goes straight in.
Settings > Start page: put your own dashboard (Homepage, Homarr...) on the start page as a button.
fixed: A website could take over Null Grid's own toolbar and sidebar if you dragged a link onto them. Now nothing can navigate Null Grid's own pages.
Passwords are now only saved and filled on secure (https) pages, only into fields you can see, and only the site (or its subdomains) they were saved for.
Websites can no longer fake a sign-in to pop up the save prompt, and a saved password can't be changed while your logins are locked.

Keep me signed in: all tabs now share one session, so sign-in pop-ups work; sites on a port (like Home Assistant :8123) stay signed in; the box starts unticked; signing out of one site no longer signs you out of others.
Updates for .deb and .rpm are checked again right before they're installed; test switches no longer work in installed copies.
"Open an app" requests now say which app, are remembered per app, and dangerous Windows tools are always refused.
Null Drive warns when its token would travel unencrypted to a network name like nas.lan.
Light theme: burner tabs are readable, new tabs no longer flash black. Cards no longer steal the keyboard while you type.

5.1.5.title: Easier on the eyes, and you stay signed in
new: Theme: Dark, Light, or Match my computer (Settings > Appearance).
Sidebar size: Large and Extra large make tab icons and text bigger, easier to see.
Save logins as you sign in: Null Grid asks Save, Not now, or Never for this site, then fills the login in next time.
Stay signed in on sites you choose (WhatsApp, GitHub...): they keep their sign-in when Null Grid closes, every other site is still wiped. Right-click a page > Keep me signed in.
This What's new card after every update, and a walkthrough with Packet the first time you open Null Grid.
fixed: A pinned tab with Masking on no longer gets stuck loading at startup.

5.1.4.title: Downloads in the toolbar
new: A download arrow in the toolbar (like Firefox): click it for your downloads, click a file to open it.
Shrunk sidebar: the icon always switches tabs; hover 2 seconds for a small close X on its corner.

5.1.3.title: Updates install themselves
new: UPDATE downloads the new version, checks it against GitHub's checksum, and installs it when you restart or close Null Grid.
fixed: 25 fixes, including the Null Drive token being sent before its certificate was checked, burner tabs leaking into history from the right-click menu, and keyboard shortcuts sometimes not working until a click.
